properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"I believe there are '3 legs' that certain skills need — have they been applied to all skills uniformly?"*

He is right that they exist. **The audit he is asking for has never been run.**

📌 DISTINCT FROM the two nodes the guard offered, and the difference is which layer is under question. `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it` MEASURES three vocabulary items against the frame. `dec:idea-how-does-a-users-project-acquire-vocabulary-it-never-uses` asks the OUTCOME question — how a project ever gets vocabulary nobody asked it for. **This asks about the INSTRUMENT: whether the three-leg test has been applied across the surface, and whether passing it means anything.** A frame can be correct, applied everywhere, and still not produce the outcome — which is exactly what the evidence below shows.

═══ WHAT THE THREE LEGS ARE ═══

For vocabulary to appear in a USER'S design, all three must be present:

1. a **TYPED TOOL** that writes it — raw `create_node`/`create_edge` does not count, since an agent must know the field exists;
2. an **INSTRUCTION**, in a served skill or tool description, saying WHEN to write it;
3. a **DETECTOR** that notices its ABSENCE, so the loop asks rather than waiting to be told.

That fact measured exactly THREE pieces of vocabulary. There are far more than three, and 22 served skills. **Nothing has ever swept the surface asking which vocabulary has which legs.**

═══ 🛑 THE SHARPER FINDING: THREE LEGS ARE NOT SUFFICIENT, AND IT IS ALREADY MEASURED TWICE ═══

**Case 1 — `DECOMPOSES`.** Typed tool ✓, instruction ✓, detector ✓ — **and the vocabulary stayed empty**, because `DecompositionCoverage` fires on a Requirement that ALREADY CARRIES an incoming DECOMPOSES edge. It checks whether an existing decomposition is covered; it cannot ask why none exists. reflow2's own graph reached **0 DECOMPOSES edges while shipping the detector for them.**

**Case 2 — half-idea linking.** `dec:idea-linking-half-ideas-needs-a-task-that-can-be-run` records that it **has all three legs and still left 110 ideas unlinked**, because nothing SUGGESTS candidates and nothing works the backlog.

⇒ Leg 3 has a hidden qualifier: *a detector that notices absence* is not the same as *a detector that notices ABSENCE OF THE WHOLE PRACTICE*. And both failures look like the same missing thing — no worklist, no runnable task, nobody's job.

⇒ **Is there a FOURTH leg: something that makes the practice HAPPEN, rather than merely possible and observable?**

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) RUN THE AUDIT AS A ONE-OFF.** Sweep every vocabulary item against the three legs, produce a table. Cheap, concrete, answers his actual question. ⚠️ Counter: a table dated today rots by next week, and a hand-taken census has been the answer several times already.

**(b) MAKE THE AUDIT A DETECTOR.** `vocabulary_coverage` already exists as a served tool — **whether it already computes something like this is UNCHECKED and should be looked at before anything is built.** ⚠️ Counter: possibly already built; look first.

**(c) NAME AND ADD THE FOURTH LEG.** Define what turns a possible practice into a performed one. ⚠️ Counter: the most speculative option here, and "nobody's job" may be a management problem rather than a design one.

**(d) RETIRE THE THREE-LEG FRAME as too coarse.** Two of its cases pass the test and fail in practice. ⚠️ Counter: it correctly diagnosed the other two cases, and a frame that catches most things is not worthless for missing some.

═══ ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT ═══

The three legs were derived from a sample of THREE. Generalising from three cases and then auditing 22 skills against it risks measuring conformance to a frame that was never validated, instead of measuring whether vocabulary actually reaches users. **The outcome that matters is "does a user's project acquire this", not "does this have three legs".**
properties.name: OPEN — the three legs were named and never audited across the surface; and two measured cases had all three and still delivered nothing
properties.rationale:
Kept separate from the tool-class question because it concerns ONE named contract that already exists, where that one asks whether kinds should carry contracts at all. This one could be answered by a sweep somebody runs this afternoon; that one cannot be answered without first deciding what the axes are.

The interesting content is not the uniformity question Anthony asked — it is that the design already holds TWO measured cases where all three legs were present and the vocabulary stayed empty. That moves the question from "have they been applied everywhere" to "is the test even the right test", and the second is worth more than the first. Recorded before checking `vocabulary_coverage`, deliberately: option (b) says look before building, and writing the question down is not the same as answering it.
